newsitem.title: USA: Gephardt--Congress should not lower CPI in budget.
newsitem.headline: Gephardt--Congress should not lower CPI in budget.

text.p: House Democratic leader Richard Gephardt said Congress should not "arbitrarily" lower the Consumer Price Index (CPI), the government's inflation gauge, as part of a budget deal with the White House.
Gephardt, who is from Missouri, told an AFL-CIO conference the government should study whether CPI overstates inflation, but Congress should not act ahead of that study.

An expert commission's finding that CPI overstates inflation by 1.1 percentage point a year is just a "theory," Gephardt told the national conference of the AFL-CIO's Building and Construction Trades Department.

"Do you really think it's a good idea for us as Congress to arbitrarily, on somebody's theory, without research being done by the Bureau of Labor Statistics ...we should go ahead and say, oh, I think this theory is right? ... I don't think so," Gephardt said.

He said the government's Bureau of Labor Statistics was willing to do the necessary research to see if the CPI is really overstating inflation. "Let's keep a system that has integrity. Let's do the research."

The commission headed by former Council of Economic Advisers chairman Michael Boskin said last December that CPI overstates inflation by 1.1 percentage point a year. The finding has led to calls for the government to reduce CPI as part of a deal to balance the federal budget, since the inflation guage is used to calculate annual increases in many federal benefit programs.
Gephardt said that if Congress voted to lower CPI it would reduce Social Security benefits for retirees by a trillion dollars over ten or 12 years.
